## Proposed change
<!--
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.
-->

The PR fixes an issue with ZHA covers, which were stuck in opening/closing state (unless top/bottom position was reached).

There is a limitation that ZCL doesn't present a standard attribute to read if cover is moving or not. The way the PR overcomes this issue is by introducing `MOVEMENT_TIMEOUT` after which the cover falls back to open/closed state. When cover is moving, the timeout is reset on every attribute report.

On top of the bugfix, there is an attempt to capture external start of movement (using wall switch) and convert them to opening/closing state as well. For this purpose, a `position_history` has been introduced.

It works fine if you use the Open/Close/Stop buttons.

review_comments:
This change (requiring both lift and tilt to be 0) would be bad for my devices. I have 4 cover devices and after completely closing them (from a completely opened state) they all report `current_position: 0` just fine, but `current_tilt_position` is reported at various values (0, 10, 15, 20).

I'm not sure if the same problem happens for `_is_open` (requiring tilt to be 100), but I can check this if needed.

The device is the one for which I opened this issue: https://github.com/zigpy/zha-device-handlers/issues/1397

Hm, it sounds like we need to agree on what "Closed" means.

On (properly calibrated) Ubisys J1, only if `tilt == 0`, it means the cover slats are really "closed". Contrary, if `lift == 0 && tilt != 0` it means there is a physical gap between slats. In extreme case, where `lift == 0 && tilt == 100`, the slats are completely horizontal, which is a confusing state to be called "Closed".

In general I agree that only `lift == 0 && tilt == 0` means "closed" (except for my note at the end of this comment). But it looks like my devices don't update the reported position often enough. So even though the physical slats are completely closed they might report a different value.

I don't know how it works exactly, but it looks like it only reports the changed tilt value every 1-2 seconds (lift values are reported way more often) and only while it's moving. So if the last reported value was 20 and then it's fully closed (stopped) before the next update interval, it will not be updated to 0. I can get it to report 0 tilt, but only for about 30% of my tries when opening/closing it.

Also, for me 100 tilt doesn't mean "slats are horizontal". They are horizontal at 50 tilt. 100 means "closed in the other direction (while opening)". So I could even say that "closed" means `lift == 0 && (tilt == 0 || tilt == 100)` (assuming my devices would report tilt correctly).

What an interesting window covering type. :)

What values of various setup attributes (as per ZCL spec chapter 7.4.2.1.3) are you using? Have you ever tried to execute any calibration procedure?

I have one of those Nexentro devices somewhere in my garage, but as far as I remember, the configuration app doesn’t allow any calibration. Nevertheless, my window coverings works differently (2-line system).

You are correct, there is no calibration.
The shutter itself only has two hardware inputs (buttons/circuits), up and down.
The app for the Zigbee device allows me to configure the time it takes for a full lift and for a full tilt. When setting a position via HA the device calculates how long it should close the up or down circuit based on the current position and target position. While the circuits are closed it emulates lift and tilt positions based on the time the circuits are closed.
You can read them one-off using ZHA Manage Device dialog: Can you please post your values of those attributes?
